purpose: Prevent exact words from becoming a shortcut around consent, de-identification, or humility.
governing_line: A quote is a living person's gift or a dead person's trace; it is not raw material.

requirements: multiple reviewed sources or contributor approval for internal pattern only
display_modes.safe_for: orientation without anecdote if not overclaiming
rare cases where words themselves are the record

requirements: high public interest or contributor desire

quote_blockers: fresh grief where contributor review is incomplete
quote creates prophecy/spiritual proof or diagnosis/prognosis impression
quote is memorable because it is sensational rather than useful
required_quote_context: who is speaking by role, not name by default
what the archive refuses to infer
paraphrase_rules: Paraphrase must not launder a quote whose exact words were not approved.
Paraphrase must preserve uncertainty and role perspective.
Paraphrase must not smooth anger, shame, conflict, humor, or ordinariness into a good-death aesthetic.
Paraphrase may be more ethical than quote when exact words are identifying or too intimate.
